guards.issue: One verdict per mechanism (binding rule 3): this is the same call-site divergence audit/records/relic/bag_of_marbles.json records as its guard G2, with the same verdict. C# targets `Enemies.Where(e => e.IsHittable)` (CombatState.cs:142), where IsHittable is `!IsDead && Hook.ShouldAllowHitting(...)`; Relic.living_enemies() (relics/base.py:294-297) filters on `not e.is_gone` only. DORMANT AT THIS SITE, and for a stronger reason than at Bag of Marbles': this relic's payload is DAMAGE, and DamageCmd.deal applies the missing predicate itself as a backstop -- `if not hooks.should_allow_hitting(target): return 0` (cmds.py:51-52) -- so an alive-but-unhittable enemy is passed in and then correctly takes nothing. Bag of Marbles routes through PowerCmd.apply, which has no such backstop (audit/records/seam/power_cmd.json gap G6), which is why the same wrong set is observable there and not here. Still recorded as a gap because the call site is wrong on both sides of the rule-3 pair and fixing PowerCmd.apply alone would not fix it; it goes live here if any effect ever reads the returned target list rather than the damage.

guards.what: G3: C# damages all enemies in ONE CreatureCmd.Damage call that defers every death to a single batched Kill(); the sim loops DamageCmd.deal per enemy, each with its own inline death processing
guards.rationale: CreatureCmd.cs:240-411 resolves the whole target list in two passes: pass 1 applies modifiers, block and HP loss to every target, and only then pass 2 fires AfterBlockBroken / AfterCurrentHpChanged / AfterDamageGiven / AfterDamageReceived per result and collects the corpses into `killedCreatures`, which a single `await Kill(killedCreatures)` at line 409 processes last. charons_ashes.py:23-27 iterates living_enemies() and calls DamageCmd.deal per enemy, and each of those calls runs its own should_die / on_death / retained_after_death block (cmds.py:96-111) before the next enemy is touched. audit/records/seam/damage_pipeline.json guard N2 already verdicts this exact structural difference deliberate-divergence and records that no concretely broken interaction was found; cited and matched under binding rule 3 rather than re-derived. It matters here specifically because Charon's Ashes is one of the sim's few genuine simultaneous-AoE sources: a ported on_death effect that damages or buffs (StockPower's Axebot spawn is the shape) would land mid-sweep in the sim and post-sweep in the game.

The `player != base.Owner` / `card.Owner != base.Owner` / `participants.Contains(base.Owner.Creature)` family is the multiplayer per-player filter on a hook the game dispatches for every player (and, for the participants form, also admits pets). The sim is single-player by construction (one RunState, one PlayerCombatState) and models no pet creature, so the filter is structurally satisfied. Multiplayer-only paths are out of scope under the shared contract.

guards.what: N1: no once-per-turn or once-per-combat limit, and `bool _` (causedByEthereal) is ignored
guards.rationale: C# fires on EVERY exhaust of an owned card, including an ethereal auto-exhaust at end of turn and including Status/Curse cards; charons_ashes.py:21 has no guard at all beyond the enemy loop. Same on both sides. Checked because the sibling relic/burning_sticks in this batch takes the same two parameters and DOES gate on card type and a once-per-combat flag -- the two relics diverge in C# too, so the sim's asymmetry is correct.

3 on both sides, no AscensionHelper call in the file. The props match exactly: valueprops.py:42 defines NON_CARD_UNPOWERED as bare `ValueProp.UNPOWERED` -- no MOVE flag -- which is what `ValueProp.Unpowered` alone means. The consequences are real and both correct: is_powered_attack is false so Strength and Vulnerable do not scale the 3 (cmds.py:55-58), and the absence of MOVE means hooks.on_attacked does NOT fire (cmds.py:69-70), so Curl Up-style on-hit powers are not triggered by the burn. Rule 7: valueprops.py and cmds.py are not hashed here.

guards.what: N3: dealer = `base.Owner.Creature`, cardSource = null on both sides
guards.rationale: charons_ashes.py:26 passes `dealer=self.player` and no card. The dealer identity is load-bearing -- it is what feeds hooks.on_damage_dealt and any Thorns retaliation -- and the null card source is what keeps card-scoped modifiers out of a relic's damage.

guards.what: N4: `self._check_win()` (charons_ashes.py:27) has no direct C# counterpart in the relic
guards.rationale: The game gets it from the CheckWinCondition that follows the enclosing action rather than from the relic body; Relic._check_win (relics/base.py:299-303) is the sim's stand-in, and its own docstring says so. Placement is right: it runs after the whole enemy loop, matching C#'s post-command check rather than a per-target one. Without it a relic that kills the last enemy would leave the combat running.

RelicModel.Flash() / FlashSfx / base.Status / ShowCounter / DisplayAmount / InvokeDisplayAmountChanged / CanonicalVars / ExtraHoverTips / Cmd.Wait / CardCmd.Preview are presentation only -- the relic bar's glow, counter, sfx and hover text, and animation timing. The sim has no relic UI. Waived under the shared contract's presentation/animation exclusion, not under an unreachability claim.
